Surah al-ʿAsr

Meccan, though according to one of the two reports from Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah, it is Medinan.

His statement, exalted is He, ﴿By time (al-ʿAṣr)﴾, this is an oath, and concerning it there are two opinions:

One of them: that al-ʿAṣr is the age (al-dahr), said by Ibn ʿAbbas and Zayd ibn Aslam.

The second: that it is the late afternoon, the period between the decline of the sun and its setting, said by al-Hasan and Qatadah, and from it is the verse of the poet:

"Set out with us in the afternoon, ʿAmr, for the afternoon has grown short, and in the first journey of the afternoon lie the spoils and the reward."

He singled it out for the oath because in it are the conclusions of deeds.

It may also admit a third meaning: that he intends the age of the Messenger (ﷺ), because of its excellence through the renewal of prophethood in it.

And there is a fourth: that he intended the afternoon prayer (ṣalat al-ʿaṣr), which is the middle prayer (al-ṣalah al-wusta), because it is the most excellent of the prayers, said by Muqatil.

﴿Indeed, mankind is surely in loss﴾: by "mankind" is meant the category of people.

Concerning "loss" (al-khusr) there are four aspects:

(p-334)

One: surely in destruction, said by al-Suddi.

The second: surely in evil, said by Zayd ibn Aslam.

The third: surely in deficiency, said by Ibn Shajarah.

The fourth: surely in punishment, and from it is the statement of the Exalted: ﴿And the consequence of their affair was loss (khusran)﴾. ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, used to recite it: "By time, and the calamities of the age, indeed mankind is in loss, and indeed he is in it until the end of the age."

﴿Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and enjoined one another to truth﴾: concerning "truth" (al-ḥaqq) there are three interpretations: One: that it is monotheism, said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: that it is the Qur'an, said by Qatadah.

The third: that it is Allah, said by al-Suddi.

It may also admit a fourth: that a person advises those he leaves behind at the approach of death not to die except as Muslims.

﴿And enjoined one another to patience﴾: concerning it there are two aspects:

One: upon the obedience of Allah, said by Qatadah.

The second: upon what Allah has made obligatory, said by Hisham ibn Hassan.

It may also admit a third interpretation: patience in refraining from what is forbidden and from following desires.
